resources.string: Before you type your disk passphrase, your Linux machine asks this phone to check it. The machine\'s TPM signs a statement of what it booted; Marify compares it with what it recorded when you bound the machine, shows you the result, and sends back a receipt signed with a key that only your fingerprint, face or screen-lock PIN can unlock.
Marify talks to your machine over Bluetooth Low Energy. It only looks for tpm2-kira machines and never uses your location.
Marify talks to your machine over Bluetooth Low Energy. On this Android version, Bluetooth scanning requires the location permission; Marify does not use your location.

Every receipt is signed with a key that needs a fresh unlock — your PIN, pattern, password, fingerprint or face — so that someone holding your unlocked phone cannot vouch for a machine without knowing your PIN.
This phone cannot protect keys with its screen lock. Marify cannot be used on it.
No machines yet. Enrol your computer to start.
Bluetooth is off. Machines asking for attestation cannot be seen.
Machines waiting for a phone appear below. Keep the computer\'s screen in view: you will compare a six-digit number.
DEBUG BUILD — not for machines you rely on
This is a debug build: it is debuggable and may keep keys outside secure hardware. Use the signed release build for machines you rely on.
Show the demo machine (simulated, no hardware needed)

Marify keeps looking for it until you cancel. The machine asks for a phone only while it shows its one-time code at boot (about 90 seconds); once it is at the passphrase prompt, it has stopped asking for this boot. If it is showing the code, it is out of range, its Bluetooth did not start, or (if you test by hand) it is not running “sudo tpm2-kira attest gate”. If its screen shows a red tpm2-kira line saying the enrolment record was not accepted, do not type your passphrase. Marify cannot say anything about this machine until it reaches it — a missing result is not a good result.
Turn on Bluetooth on this phone. Marify continues looking for %1$s as soon as it is on.
The machine will be told that you cancelled.
Does this match the number on your computer\'s screen?
The machine\'s TPM proved it holds an endorsement key certified by its manufacturer.
TPM not verified as genuine hardware
This version of Marify can verify TPMs from: %1$s.

Marify could not confirm that this machine\'s TPM is real hardware (%1$s). This is common for firmware TPMs without a usable certificate. Only continue if you trust the machine\'s current state: a machine that is already compromised could pretend to have a TPM.
The checked boot measurements do not include the initrd

On this boot the initrd was measured into PCR %1$s, which this enrolment does not check. A modified initrd, for example one that records your passphrase, would then show as unchanged. Cancel, and enrol again with “--pcrs” including PCR %1$s.
The checked boot measurements include the initrd (PCR %1$s).
The machine could not tell where its initrd was measured. Make sure the checked PCRs cover it.
This machine boots without an initrd.
For this machine the screen-lock PIN will not be enough. Changing it later means enrolling the machine again.
Unlocked by fingerprint, face or screen-lock PIN
Unlocked by fingerprint or face only
From now on, when this machine boots and waits for attestation, Marify will show it here.
Do not type your passphrase unless you know why:
A hard check failed. Approving tells the machine that this boot is trusted. Type the machine\'s name, %1$s, to confirm.
Reset count %1$d · restart count %2$d · firmware %3$d · clock safe: %4$s
The machine says the receipt is not from its enrolled phone.
The machine says the receipt does not belong to this session.
The machine could not read the receipt.

The machine asks this phone to keep one half of its disk key: a sealed value only its own TPM can open, in a boot it has approved. Accepting this verdict keeps it, replacing any kept before. From then on it is handed back after every verdict you accept, and the machine needs it together with your password to unlock the disk.
This machine takes no disk factor.
The machine\'s TPM refused to open the factor: this boot is not one its owner approved.
The machine had no accepted receipt for it.
Kept on this phone since %1$s. Only the machine\'s TPM can open it.
None kept. Run \"tpm2-kira factor enrol\" on the machine to add one.
The machine is advertising as yours but refused the secure connection, twice. Its enrolment data was changed or removed, or this is a different machine imitating it.
Do not type your passphrase. If you did not change the enrolment yourself (for example by running “attest enrol” with another phone), treat the machine as tampered with.
Marify reached the machine, but setting up the connection failed.
This machine speaks a different protocol version. Please update the app or tpm2-kira.
The machine is not in the expected mode. For enrolment run \'attest enrol\'; for verification, \'attest gate\'.
The numbers did not match, so nothing was stored. Someone may be interfering; try again in a different place.
Cancelled at the unlock check. Nothing was signed.
The key for this machine was invalidated because the phone\'s fingerprints, face or screen lock changed. Delete the machine and enrol it again.
The machine could not be stored on this phone.
This phone is not enrolled with the machine
Credential activation failed: the TPM could not prove its key
The stored policy for this machine is invalid.
The machine\'s attestation key is not the one it enrolled with.
The TPM signature does not verify.
The quote was not produced by a TPM.
The TPM produced something other than a quote.
The quote was not made for this session; it may be replayed.
The TPM\'s boot counter went backwards: a replayed quote or a cleared TPM.
The machine claimed to hold its boot key but could not prove it.
New to this phone, but signed by the machine\'s TPM as approved by its owner.
The machine must show the same code.
No code: the TPM did not release the boot key. This boot state is not approved by the machine\'s owner (an update not yet resealed, or asked after the code screen).
No code: the machine could not answer with its boot key.
The TPM\'s clock is not trustworthy.
The machine reported different registers than requested.
The reported register values are invalid.
The reported register values are not the ones the TPM signed.
The boot chain differs from every state you approved.
The machine booted several times since the last check.
The TPM\'s clock is not trustworthy.
Signs a receipt with this phone\'s key
Unlock for every signature, enforced by secure hardware
